answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through hardware-enforced remote attestation. Acting as a cryptographic velvet rope, nodes must run inside secure enclaves that generate signed quotes of unique execution before joining the agent garden. This anchors identities in a verifiable hardware orchard, forcing an attacker to dedicate scarce physical silicon chips per instance. However, this approach centralizes trust in hardware vendor root keys and remains vulnerable to side-channel extraction.
